name: RiddoDuottarMuseat
funding: 2023: about NOK 15M in public operating grants, NOK 13.1M of it from the Sámi Parliament (Sametinget), plus Finnmark county and four municipalities.
watch: A Sámi museum foundation running several sites.
records_note: RDM posts annual reports for 2014 to 2025 and names its eight board members, but no donor list; its accounts are in Norway's register.

name: Nordnorsk Kunstmuseum
watch: The regional art museum for Northern Norway, with a strong Sámi programme. It opened a Bodø venue in 2025 and programmes Nordover in Longyearbyen.
records_note: The museum names its 2024 to 2027 board and files accounts in Norway's register, but posts no annual reports and no funder list.

name: Bishop Museum (Bernice Pauahi Bishop Museum)
funding: 2023 revenue US$21.5M (IRS 990), from state and federal agencies, Hawai'i foundations such as Kamehameha Schools, and Hawai'i corporate sponsors.
watch: Hawai'i's state museum of natural and cultural history, founded in memory of Princess Bernice Pauahi Bishop.
records_note: The museum posts annual reports for 2020 to 2025, audited statements and Form 990s, named corporate and foundation donors, and its board of directors.

name: Vanuatu Cultural Centre (Vanuatu Kaljoral Senta)
funding: A small statutory body funded by the Vanuatu government. After the Dec 2024 earthquake it relied on UNESCO's Heritage Emergency Fund (to May 2026) and online fundraising.
watch: Vanuatu's national museum, archive and fieldworker network. The Dec 2024 quake broke cases and destroyed Lapita pottery.
records_note: The centre's site posts no annual reports, accounts, named funders or board; its 2025 newsletter names funding types only.

name: Solomon Islands National Museum
funding: A small government museum under the Ministry of Culture and Tourism. In 2024 its virtual museum was funded by Australia's Digital Pasifik project with UK support.
watch: Founded in 1969 and a government institution since 1972. It went online in Oct 2024 with help from the New Zealand and Australian national libraries.
records_note: The museum has no site of its own and its government portal pages returned errors, so its reports, accounts, funders and board are unchecked.

name: HEK (Haus der Elektronischen Künste)
funding: Small foundation-run house (2025); carried by the Christoph Merian Stiftung, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft and the Federal Office of Culture.
watch: Building is at Freilager-Platz 9 in Münchenstein. Education is funded by Göhner and Binding; the Pax Art Awards by Art Foundation Pax, an insurer's foundation.
records_note: HEK posts annual reports for 2021 to 2025 and names its foundation board, but shows funders as logos and publishes no accounts.

name: iMAL
funding: Small art-and-tech centre (2025) with structural funding from Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles, Flanders and VGC, plus the National Lottery and the ERDF.
watch: Canal-side centre and fablab in Molenbeek. Its private partners are Fondation Orange (telecom) and Selligent (software).
records_note: iMAL names its board and shows public and private partners as logos, but posts no annual reports or accounts.

name: Kapelica Gallery (Kersnikova Institute)
funding: Small NGO venue (2025), funded by Slovenia's Ministry of Culture, the City of Ljubljana and EU programmes.
watch: Research-art gallery founded in 1995 by the Student Organisation of the University of Ljubljana (ŠOU). Run by Kersnikova with the BioTehna lab and the Rampa hacker space.
records_note: Kersnikova lists 21 supporters by name but posts no annual reports, accounts or board; its Crew page names a director and staff.

name: NTT InterCommunication Center (ICC)
funding: Corporate cultural facility (2026) run and paid for by NTT East, a telecom operator, in Tokyo Opera City Tower.
watch: Opened in 1997 to mark the centenary of Japan's telephone service. A non-profit art and science venue, not a commercial attraction.
records_note: ICC publishes nothing itself; its operator NTT East posts annual financial results and names its directors, and ICC lists no funders.

name: transmediale
funding: Annual festival (2026) funded since 2004 by the Kulturstiftung des Bundes. Berlin Senate, bpb, Medienboard and Creative Europe funding was listed for 2020–21.
watch: Coordinates mark central Berlin, because festival venues change each year. Its 2026 partner programmes include the Schering Stiftung and HAU.
records_note: transmediale names no board and posts no reports or accounts; its old partner page shows funder logos and its about page names two funders.

name: LABoral Centro de Arte y Creación Industrial
funding: Public foundation (budget about €1.3M in 2014) governed by Asturias, Gijón city and the Gijón Port Authority. Project sponsors in 2023 included the Onassis Foundation's Ariona Hellas.
watch: Housed in the Universidad Laboral building. Fundación EDP, an energy group's foundation, co-funded the Eco-Visionarios exhibition in 2018–19.
records_note: LABoral posts activity reports for 2018 to 2025, audited accounts for 2014 to 2025 and its trustees, but no list of named funders.

name: Eyebeam
funding: Small nonprofit (revenue $1.63M in 2023), funded by Atlantic, Ford, Jerome and Arison Arts foundations, the NEA, NYSCA and NYC DCLA.
watch: Art-and-technology nonprofit registered in Brooklyn as Eyebeam Atelier Inc. Arison Arts Foundation is Arison-family money.
records_note: Eyebeam's support page names its institutional funders, individual donors and seven board members; its Form 990s are public, but it posts no annual reports.
